title: High-pressure alarm and falling tidal volumes
summary: A ventilated 58-year-old man has a high peak pressure alarm, small returned breaths and a rising CO2.
rationale: A partial tube or large-airway plug raises resistance but not compliance, so Ppk rises while Pplat stays near 18; it also slows exhalation. Suction restores resistance. Headless engine check on the starting settings and after the named actions: untouched by 2 min: PaCO2 49, pH 7.31, SpO2 94%, Pplat 19, auto-PEEP 0.6, SBP 106; untouched by 30 min: PaCO2 55, pH 7.27, SpO2 94%, Pplat 19, auto-PEEP 0.6, SBP 106; reasonable management by 30 min: PaCO2 52, pH 7.30, SpO2 94%, Pplat 18, SBP 110; typical mistake by 30 min: PaCO2 37, pH 7.41, SpO2 94%, Pplat 21, auto-PEEP 2.5, SBP 101. Values for an arm whose case ended early (improved or deteriorated trigger) are the values when it ended.

retestsMistake.clinicalFocus: High peak with a normal plateau means resistance: suction and check the tube before searching for exotic causes

source: The Ventilator Book 3e (alarms / troubleshooting and respiratory mechanics chapters, numbers unverified); Marino ICU Book 2025 (ventilator-associated complications and airway pressure chapters, unverified); Nunn & Lumb 9e (resistance and compliance chapters, unverified); Hess DR. Respir Care 2014;59:1773-94 (peak minus plateau pressure); Resistance 26 cmH2O/L/s and expiratory resistance 28 are teaching assumptions for a partly occluded tube (unverified).

changes.vignette: Male 58, 172 cm, 75 kg. VC 420 mL, RR 16, PEEP 8, FiO2 0.4. Tube resistance high from inspissated secretions.

patient.presentingStory: Intubated for pneumonia 3 days ago, on VC 420 mL. The high-pressure alarm has been sounding on and off and the nurse notes thick secretions overnight. Blood pressure is acceptable.
patient.history: Pneumonia with thick secretions, dry humidifier overnight. Full escalation.

findings.examine: Sedated. Equal chest movement, coarse transmitted sounds, no wheeze. The suction catheter meets resistance 8 cm into the tube. Tube at 22 cm at the teeth.
findings.cxr: Tube 4 cm above the carina, right lower zone consolidation, both lungs expanded, no pneumothorax.

evidence.claim: A partly obstructed tube raises peak pressure but not plateau pressure; suction clears the plug and restores flow.
evidence.source: Marino PL. Marino's The ICU Book, 2025 edition (chapter on ventilator troubleshooting; number unverified)

evidence.claim: Measurement of plateau pressure via inspiratory hold differentiates high resistance (elevated Ppeak, normal Pplat) from low compliance (both Ppeak and Pplat elevated).
evidence.source: Hess DR. Respiratory mechanics in the mechanically ventilated patient. Respir Care 2014;59(11):1773-1794

orderEffects.note: Removing the plug restores airway resistance

actions.text: A thick mucus plug is suctioned from the tube. The peak pressure falls and the tidal volume returns.
Salbutamol given through the circuit. There is no obvious change in the airway pressures.
The senior says: what do the peak and plateau pressures show, and where does the tube sit? Work through the DOPE checklist.
Furosemide 40 mg given and the urine output rises a little. There is no immediate change in the airway pressures.

then.reason: The cause of the high airway pressure was found and treated; pressures, blood pressure and oxygenation have recovered.
The high airway pressure was not corrected, and the patient became profoundly hypotensive or hypoxaemic.

then.detail: A high peak airway pressure persisted for 7 minutes without a structured check (DOPE: tube, obstruction, pneumothorax, equipment) and an inspiratory hold to separate resistance from compliance.

rubric.description: Examined the patient within 8 minutes of the alarm
Brought peak pressure to 32 cmH2O or below
Checked a blood gas within 20 minutes

keyPoints: Peak pressure high with a normal plateau pressure means a resistance problem (secretions, kinked or bitten tube); both high means a compliance problem.
Suction and a suction-catheter pass are the first step for a suspected obstructed airway; do not wait for imaging.
Treating the alarm by raising the rate in an obstructed patient worsens air trapping.
